page_title: Ultravox.ai — Real-time, speech native voice AI

summary.name: Ultravox
summary.one_liner: Ultravox is a real-time, speech-native voice AI infrastructure layer for building fast, natural voice agents, now acquired by Inworld according to the page banner.
use_cases: building voice agents for customer conversations
adding voice to web or mobile apps
telephony voice agents over phone calls
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Ultravox as a speech-native voice AI stack that avoids converting speech to text before LLM processing, arguing this preserves tone, cadence and pitch and reduces latency. It says the company trains its own speech model (Ultravox v0.7) and runs its own inference and infrastructure rather than relying on external LLMs. It offers developer REST APIs, SDKs for web and mobile, built-in tools, and telephony provider integrations. It also lists UltraVAD v0.1, a neural voice activity model for turn-taking and endpointing, and reports Ultravox v0.7 scoring 91.8% on Big Bench Audio without reasoning and 97% with thinking enabled.
notable: Speech-native model that processes audio directly instead of transcribing to text first
Open weight models with research sharing
UltraVAD neural turn-taking and endpointing model
Ultravox v0.7 benchmark score of 91.8% without reasoning and 97% with thinking on Big Bench Audio
caveats: Free tier is 5 cents per minute for up to 5 concurrent calls; Pro is $100/month (billed yearly) with no hard concurrency caps; Enterprise is custom pricing
Speech generation is listed as coming soon
Page banner says Ultravox has been acquired by Inworld, so the product's future may change
